title.narrative: Leveraging Interfaith Mechanism for Conflict Mitigation (LIMCO)

description.narrative:
The Inter-Religious Council of Kenya (IRCK), through the Marsabit Interfaith Council (MIC), proposes a faith-led peacebuilding intervention aimed at addressing the causes of these conflict through mediation and dialogue Drawing on community-led conflict and risk analyses conducted by religious leaders, elders, women, and youth, the project will focus on conflict resolution by religious leaders through four pathways namely; strengthening capacity of MIC, strengthening early warning and response mechanism, building social cohesion and advocacy and strategic linkages. The project will benefit conflict-affected communities across Saku and Moyale sub-counties directly and all other sub-counties in Marsabit County indirectly, with particular focus on youth, women, elders, religious leaders, community leaders, political leaders and peace and security actors as agents of peace.
Aligned with Christian Aid and Islamic Relief's aspiration to strengthen and build faith partnerships, the project builds on IRCK’s proven experience in peacebuilding and advocacy, and on the Marsabit Interfaith Council’s moral legitimacy, convening capacity, and strong community presence to promote locally led, conflict-sensitive, and sustainable peace outcomes.
